title: Partition Array into Disjoint Intervals
summary: Given an integer array nums, divide it into two contiguous subarrays left and right such that every element in left is less than or equal to every element in right, both subarrays are non-empty, and left is as small as possible.
statement: Given an integer array nums, divide it into two contiguous subarrays left and right such that every element in left is less than or equal to every element in right, both subarrays are non-empty, and left is as small as possible. Return the length of the left subarray after partitioning.
constraints: A valid split exists with nonempty left and right parts.
Return the smallest left length where every left value is at most every right value.
hints: Track the maximum committed to the left and the maximum seen overall.
When a new value is below left_max, the split must move past it.
Set answer=i+1 and promote left_max to global_max.
Each violation forces inclusion; otherwise all later values seen remain at least the committed maximum.
editorial: Each violation forces inclusion; otherwise all later values seen remain at least the committed maximum.

tests.explanation: The first three values have maximum five, no greater than the remaining minimum six.
The smallest valid left part ends after the zero, at length four.
